96 Plus, Southwest is opening lounges, and American goes all in on big spenders   Is this email difficult to read? View in browser             Sponsored by       Dawn Gilbertson   Travel Hacks You (Probably) Haven’t Heard Before   Plus, Southwest is opening lounges, and American goes all in on big spenders   Happy Friday and happy last blast of summer unless you live in a state where summer sticks around until Halloween. The truest sign vacation season is over: Take a gander at the cuckoo hotel rates in New York City next week. A Marriott Courtyard for $920? No, thanks. 

   The big news in travel this week: Southwest Airlines is finally joining the airport-lounge game. The airline plans to open its first four lounges in Baltimore, Nashville, Austin, Texas, and Honolulu in partnership with Chase. The airline revealed scant details on the lounges, including who gets in besides the holders of a premium credit card that will launch next year. Oh, and it won’t be called the LUV Shack, much to my colleague Aly Sider’s chagrin. The first lounge isn’t due to open until the end of 2027 so don’t get too excited. 

   If you ever doubted airlines’ laser focus on big-spending travelers, check out the makeover American Airlines announced for its Boeing 777-300ER in Dallas this week. There are 70 Flagship business class suites, 44 premium economy seats and 30 Main Cabin Extra seats, giving the plane the most premium seats on any U.S. airline, it says. The business-class seats are similar to those I flew on the airline’s new Boeing 787 Dreamliner from Philadelphia to London a year ago. 

   JetBlue Airways threw out a few more details on its new first-class cabin , including custom-cocktail ordering from your seat back screen. Routes and pricing information won’t be out until later this year. 

   United announced that it is testing food delivery to the gate in Newark, and Carnival Cruise Line is borrowing a page from airlines and switching to a spending-based loyalty program . 

   On a somber note, two people died and at least one hiker is still missing after devastating flash flooding in the Grand Canyon. 

       Travel hacks you can use on your next trip     Pro tip: Buy your travel snacks in advance. This stash cost around $30 at the airport. DAWN GILBERTSON/WSJ   You don’t have to scroll far on social media to find travel hacks from influencers, wannabe influencers, travel agents, frequent fliers and people trying to sell you something. Some are complete B.S. and some get repeated over and over, but you can find some gems you might not have considered.

   I came across a post on Threads this week with this prompt: “Tell me your best ‘nobody tells travelers’ this tip. Not ‘roll your clothes.’ I mean the weirdly specific thing you learned from actually traveling. The kind of tip that makes someone say: ‘WHY did nobody tell me that before?’”

   More than 3,000 people commented. Dulles Airport even weighed in, saying starting out at the right airport helps ! (Travelers routinely get it mixed up with Washington Reagan National.)

   Here are a few that were newish to me and not mentioned in my hotel wish list and hotel hacks columns.

   • Use inexpensive battery-operated tea lights as nightlights in hotel rooms.

   • Use the restroom at baggage claim because no one is ever there.

   • Take a photo at the end of the trip of stuff you packed but never used. Refer to it next time you pack. (I can relate to this example the traveler posted: “For some reason, for many trips, I’d convinced myself that I’d do a sheet mask each night and use all the little product samples I’d collected, like Sephora samples.”

   • Pack the random snack that you don’t eat often, but occasionally crave on the road. And buy it at the dollar store instead of spending $15 on Cheetos at the airport.

   • Don’t pack “what if” items like umbrellas. You can buy them anywhere. 

   • Treat yourself to a spa treatment or food tour on the first day while you’re waiting for your room.

   Send me yours via email at dawn.gilbertson@wsj.com (if you’re reading this in your inbox, you can just hit reply). Remember, it isn’t supposed to be a retread, e.g. put one shoe you’re wearing home in the hotel safe so you don’t forget your passport and other valuables.

   I’ll start: For early morning flights, order espresso on ice and add in a protein shake. Voilà, you have a breakfast-and-caffeine fix in one.

   This is an edition of the WSJ Travel newsletter, a weekly source of inspiration and advice for navigating your vacations and business trips, along with the latest travel news. If you’re not subscribed, sign up here . 

       Notes From the Road ✈️     PETER ARKLE FOR WSJ   • Check out my guide to all those airport line-cutting options . (I also talked about it on our What’s News podcast .) 

   • Feel like you’re not getting enough value out of your pricey travel credit card? You’re not alone .

   • Our China correspondent enjoyed one of the best high-end Chinese meals of her life. It was in Taiwan , not Beijing or Shanghai. 

   • The man who created the chic Soho House clubs is opening a London hotel . 

   • Maine oyster season reaches its peak just as summer crowds disperse.

       CONTENT FROM: SILVERSEA CRUISES     SILVERSEA BRINGS THE WORLD CLOSER   Explore over 900 destinations across all seven continents on board small ships that set the standard for elite ocean travel. From the Mediterranean and the Caribbean to Antarctica and the Galápagos, Silversea voyages are defined by immersive exploration, personalized service, all-inclusive indulgence, culinary innovation, and unmatched access to the world.   Discover More  >       One Good Tip 🎯   Want to accompany a friend or family member to their gate or greet them upon arrival? You can now do that at 13 airports across the country if you have TSA PreCheck and register in advance. The TSA’s new Gateside by TSA PreCheck launched this week. This is different from those airport visitor pass programs .

       Travel Math 🧮   $244,000   The overdue bill Los Angeles County sent to Amazon founder Jeff Bezos for taxes and fees on his luxury jet, according to the Los Angeles Times. The county assessor is cracking down on celebrity jet owners.

       And We Quote 💬   “Today we’re not in the decision set for a lot of customers who need connectivity. And that will change next year.”

   — New Frontier Airlines CEO Jimmy Dempsey on the discount airline’s plans to add Starlink Wi-Fi . He didn’t say whether it will be free.

       You Have Thoughts 🤔   …on airport line-cutting options . 

   • “Your article sorting out airport pre-check alternatives was very helpful and much appreciated. Just wish you had added Nexus for those whose foreign travel includes regular trips to Canada. I live in Ohio and travel to Canada frequently and usually find myself in a line of cars at the border, gazing longingly at the empty Nexus line.” — Kenneth Wear, Ohio 

   • “The Global Entry pass has the added benefit of allowing travelers driving from Mexico into the U.S. to use the Sentri auto lanes at the border crossing. On our biannual driving trips to our place in Baja, this has turned an hour or two or longer wait in line when crossing back into the U.S. into 15 minutes or less.” — Bill Waggener, California  

   • “I’ve had TSA PreCheck for years and now do the Touchless ID as well. I tried Clear a while back and dropped it. There is, though, something unsavory to me about paying for an expedite of a government service. Almost like paying the local fire department a fee so that they come to my house more quickly than my neighbor’s if there’s an emergency.” — Garrett Calhoun, California 

   (Responses have been condensed and edited.) 

       Cheers and Jeers 🤷   Cheers to Chase for finally expanding its tiny new lounge at Phoenix Sky Harbor International Airport (though it no longer accepts reservations). A friend visited Thursday and says she breezed right in. I’ll put it to the test next week and report back.

   Jeers to airlines and hotels that make it too hard to track down receipts. It shouldn’t be this hard to fill out an expense report.

Travel Hacks You (Probably) Haven’t Heard Before
 
Plus, Southwest is opening lounges, and American goes all in on big spenders
 

Happy Friday and happy last blast of summer unless you live in a state where summer sticks around until Halloween. The truest sign vacation season is over: Take a gander at the cuckoo hotel rates in New York City next week. A Marriott Courtyard for $920? No, thanks.

Oh, and it won’t be called the LUV Shack, much to my colleague Aly Sider’s chagrin. The first lounge isn’t due to open until the end of 2027 so don’t get too excited.

On a somber note, two people died and at least one hiker is still missing after devastating flash flooding in the Grand Canyon.

 
 
 

Travel hacks you can use on your next trip

 
 
Pro tip: Buy your travel snacks in advance. This stash cost around $30 at the airport. DAWN GILBERTSON/WSJ
 

You don’t have to scroll far on social media to find travel hacks from influencers, wannabe influencers, travel agents, frequent fliers and people trying to sell you something. Some are complete B.S. and some get repeated over and over, but you can find some gems you might not have considered.

 

I came across a post on Threads this week with this prompt: “Tell me your best ‘nobody tells travelers’ this tip. Not ‘roll your clothes.’ I mean the weirdly specific thing you learned from actually traveling. The kind of tip that makes someone say: ‘WHY did nobody tell me that before?’”

 

More than 3,000 people commented. Dulles Airport even weighed in, saying starting out at the right airport helps! (Travelers routinely get it mixed up with Washington Reagan National.)

 

Here are a few that were newish to me and not mentioned in my hotel wish list and hotel hacks columns.

 

• Use inexpensive battery-operated tea lights as nightlights in hotel rooms.

 

• Use the restroom at baggage claim because no one is ever there.

(I can relate to this example the traveler posted: “For some reason, for many trips, I’d convinced myself that I’d do a sheet mask each night and use all the little product samples I’d collected, like Sephora samples.”

Send me yours via email at dawn.gilbertson@wsj.com (if you’re reading this in your inbox, you can just hit reply). Remember, it isn’t supposed to be a retread, e.g. put one shoe you’re wearing home in the hotel safe so you don’t forget your passport and other valuables.

 

I’ll start: For early morning flights, order espresso on ice and add in a protein shake. Voilà, you have a breakfast-and-caffeine fix in one.

Notes From the Road ✈️

 
 
PETER ARKLE FOR WSJ
 

• Check out my guide to all those airport line-cutting options. (I also talked about it on our What’s News podcast.)

One Good Tip 🎯

 

Want to accompany a friend or family member to their gate or greet them upon arrival? You can now do that at 13 airports across the country if you have TSA PreCheck and register in advance. The TSA’s new Gateside by TSA PreCheck launched this week. This is different from those airport visitor pass programs.

 
 
 

Travel Math 🧮

 
$244,000
 

The overdue bill Los Angeles County sent to Amazon founder Jeff Bezos for taxes and fees on his luxury jet, according to the Los Angeles Times. The county assessor is cracking down on celebrity jet owners.

 
 
 

And We Quote 💬

 

“Today we’re not in the decision set for a lot of customers who need connectivity. And that will change next year.”

 

— New Frontier Airlines CEO Jimmy Dempsey on the discount airline’s plans to add Starlink Wi-Fi. He didn’t say whether it will be free.

 
 
 

You Have Thoughts 🤔

 

…on airport line-cutting options.

 

• “Your article sorting out airport pre-check alternatives was very helpful and much appreciated. Just wish you had added Nexus for those whose foreign travel includes regular trips to Canada. I live in Ohio and travel to Canada frequently and usually find myself in a line of cars at the border, gazing longingly at the empty Nexus line.” —Kenneth Wear, Ohio

 

• “The Global Entry pass has the added benefit of allowing travelers driving from Mexico into the U.S. to use the Sentri auto lanes at the border crossing. On our biannual driving trips to our place in Baja, this has turned an hour or two or longer wait in line when crossing back into the U.S. into 15 minutes or less.” —Bill Waggener, California 

 

• “I’ve had TSA PreCheck for years and now do the Touchless ID as well. I tried Clear a while back and dropped it. There is, though, something unsavory to me about paying for an expedite of a government service. Almost like paying the local fire department a fee so that they come to my house more quickly than my neighbor’s if there’s an emergency.” —Garrett Calhoun, California

 

(Responses have been condensed and edited.)

Jeers to airlines and hotels that make it too hard to track down receipts. It shouldn’t be this hard to fill out an expense report.
